uk-cpi-2026-10.standing: The Office for National Statistics' monthly measure of how fast prices are rising for UK households. The Bank of England targets it at 2%, so it steers interest rates, and benefit and pension increases are tied to it.
uk-cpi-2026-10.recent: Economists have warned of 5% UK inflation if a US diesel ban goes ahead, which turns attention to the fuel and energy lines of this release rather than the headline rate alone. The September figure reports prices as they stood while that ban was still a proposal, and it sets the baseline the warning is measured against.

fomc-2026-10.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the target for overnight lending between US banks. Its decision moves borrowing costs for every dollar debtor, in the US and far beyond it.
fomc-2026-10.recent: Hiring of 29,000 in September against 90,000 expected sets a stalling labour market against the Hormuz energy shock the committee has been raising rates to fight. Dallas Fed president Lorie Logan says more rises are needed. Trump demanded Powell resign after a watchdog cleared him, leaving the vote itself contested.

ecb-2026-10.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which meets roughly every six weeks to set interest rates for the countries sharing the euro. Its decisions reach borrowing costs for some 350 million people, and the euro moves with them.
ecb-2026-10.recent: Euro zone inflation jumped to 3.8% in September from 3.2%, and Lagarde has described a darkening picture. The council weighs a rate rise against an imported energy shock it cannot reach: higher rates raise borrowing costs for the bloc's most indebted governments, and France's premium over Germany is already at its widest in 14 years.

boj-2026-10.standing: Japan's central bank, whose policy board meets eight times a year to set the short-term interest rate. Its decisions move the yen, the cost of Japan's vast public debt, and the flow of Japanese savings into foreign bonds.
boj-2026-10.recent: The Bank of Japan raised its rate in September to curb rising prices, and Japanese yields have jumped since, deepening a global bond sell-off. This meeting settles whether that hike was a single step or the start of a faster run, and how much more strain the board is prepared to put on its own government-debt market.

boe-2026-11.standing: The Bank of England's nine-member Monetary Policy Committee, which meets eight times a year to set Bank Rate. Its vote feeds through to mortgage and savings rates across Britain, and sterling and gilt yields move with it.
boe-2026-11.recent: The committee decides with its peers already turning: Japan raised its rate to a 31-year high and Lagarde painted a darkening picture of inflation in Europe. The global bond sell-off reached London too, with the FTSE 100 set to fall as yields hit multiyear highs. This meeting settles where the Bank of England stands in that shift.

fomc-2026-12.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the target for overnight lending between US banks. Its decisions price dollar borrowing worldwide, from US mortgages to emerging-market debt.
fomc-2026-12.recent: The committee has been raising rates against energy inflation from the Hormuz shock, which rate rises cannot fix, and September's 29,000 new jobs against 90,000 expected show hiring already stalling. Dallas Fed's Lorie Logan says more rises are needed. Trump has demanded Powell resign after a watchdog cleared him, leaving who votes in question.

g20-2026-miami.standing: The yearly meeting of leaders from 19 major economies plus the European Union and African Union, hosted by a rotating presidency that sets the agenda. Its members produce about 85% of world output, and it decides by consensus.
g20-2026-miami.recent: Rubio has invited Putin, who is wanted by the ICC, to Miami, and the Kremlin is weighing the invitation. Its answer sets what the summit is about before any agenda item: whether the other leaders sit at a table with him, and whether a host's invitation counts for more than the court's.

ecb-2026-12.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which meets eight times a year to set interest rates for every country sharing the euro. Its decisions reach mortgages, government borrowing costs and the euro's exchange rate.
ecb-2026-12.recent: Euro zone inflation jumped to 3.8% in September from 3.2%, against a 2% target, and Lagarde has painted a darkening picture. The bind is that a hike aimed at an energy shock imported since the Hormuz disruption raises borrowing costs for the bloc's most indebted governments, and France's premium over Germany is already its widest in 14 years.

boe-2026-12.standing: The Bank of England's nine-member Monetary Policy Committee, which meets eight times a year to set Bank Rate. Its vote reaches British mortgages and business loans within weeks, and sterling and gilt yields move with it.
boe-2026-12.recent: The committee decides with its peers already tightening: Japan raised its rate to a 31-year high, Australia's inflation has defied a run of rate hikes, and Lagarde has described a darkening inflation picture in Europe. The meeting settles whether the Bank of England moves with them or holds apart.

boj-2026-12.standing: Japan's central bank, whose policy board meets eight times a year to set the short-term interest rate. Its decisions move the yen and the yield on Japanese government bonds, one of the largest pools of debt in the world.
boj-2026-12.recent: The Bank of Japan raised its rate in September to curb rising prices, and Japanese bond yields have since jumped, deepening a global bond sell-off. This meeting decides whether the board tightens again while that sell-off is still running — the cost of fighting inflation is now landing on Japan's own debt market.
